evidence: Liv. 2.12.9: et facere et patī fortia Rōmānum est
terms.comment: Also “allow”: patī ab igne ignem capere, to let someone light a fire from yours (Cic. Off. 1.52).

evidence: Catull. 8.11: sed obstinātā mente perfer, obdūrā

terms.gloss: suffer, receive (a wrong, a defeat, a loss)
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 5.56: accipere quam facere praestat injūriam
Traupman 186: clādem accipere, to suffer a defeat
terms.comment: Of what one is dealt: injūriam, clādem accipere. To suffer a loss: damnum facere (see loss).

evidence: Ter. Ph. 138: quod fors feret, ferēmus aequō animō

terms.gloss: put up with, bear patiently, endure to the end
evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.77: facile omnēs perpetior ac perferō (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 106: put up with s.o., aliquem perpetior
Plaut. Am. 3.2.1: dūrāre nequeō in aedibus (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: last, hold out to the end

phrases.latin: et facere et patī fortia Rōmānum est
phrases.english: to act bravely and to suffer bravely is the Roman way

phrases.latin: nunc patior nivēs imbrēsque in silvīs asperam vītam trahēns
phrases.english: as it is, I put up with snow and rain in the woods, dragging out a hard life
it is better to suffer a wrong than to do one

phrases.latin: quod acerbum fuit ferre, tulisse jūcundum est
phrases.english: what was hard to bear is pleasant to have borne
